tasks.short: Interpret QC results and recommend data release

steps.what: Verify test results and select established specifications and control limits for comparison
Compare recorded test results with the selected established specifications and control limits
Interpret test results and recommend whether the data are appropriate for release

tasks.design: Configure fixed comparisons in {OTHER}, the laboratory information management system, using the analyst's checked result and limit references. The analyst interprets the full test context and accepts a release recommendation; the system does not release data or products.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated numerical comparison was mixed with the harder assessment of result validity and significance.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit limits, units and comparison rules can be configured and tested independently of interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: A result within limits can still be unsuitable because of sampling, method or data-integrity concerns.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst understands why a result is credible and when further investigation is required.
tasks.altitude: Less fixed-limit arithmetic; interpretation and release recommendation responsibility remain human.

evidence.claim: Fixed numerical comparisons can be configured separately from interpretation; the proposed savings are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is interpretation, established-limit comparison and the analyst's release recommendation, excluding performing tests, general data compilation and final authorized release. Each comparison must have one owner across QC tasks.

Testing staff and instruments produce sample identifier, method version, analyte, result, unit, timestamp and source record through unchanged testing. Specification owners produce versioned limits through existing controlled work; additional structured-field upkeep is counted below.

Analyst verifies and captures result references, applicable specification and control-limit versions, units, lower and upper limits, inclusive boundaries, rounding and missing-result treatment in s1's 25 hours. Applicability and capture are not free structured inputs.

Missing limits, incompatible units, censored results or uncertain methods remain unresolved and return to manual comparison and investigation in s3's 55 hours. No machine flag establishes validity or release appropriateness.

Test native laboratory configuration first. Customer quality requirements determine validation and approval needs; s3 retains meaning checks and the exact recommendation, while final release remains existing downstream work.
unknowns: Whether native comparisons can represent the applicable methods and limits
Which quality validation and approval requirements apply
research_questions: Do configured comparisons reproduce prior decisions while leaving invalid or ambiguous results visibly unresolved?

already_counted.description: Select and capture applicable limits, interpret results and resolve comparison exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain comparison definitions and retest method changes
Maintain additional result and specification fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact recommendation, result snapshot, method and specification versions, comparison rules and unresolved concerns; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80, gross=20; subtract 8 focal upkeep for central net=12. Range assumes partial fixed-rule coverage and substantial manual exceptions. Three other-role upkeep hours are outside focal savings; no testing or final release time is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Perform visual inspections of finished products and record observed defects and uncertainty

tasks.design: Keep visual inspection human, using {OTHER}, the laboratory inspection record system, to retain observations where currently used. No camera installation, automated defect classifier or reduction in handling time is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual appearance and ambiguous defects require observation of the finished item.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing native criteria and records support the inspection without new hardware.
tasks.still_hard: Lighting, subtle variation and context can change what an apparent defect means.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst notices unexpected features and investigates rather than forcing them into a known label.
tasks.altitude: Inspection time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Observe product appearance against documented criteria

evidence.claim: Visual product inspection requires direct observation; no labour saving or untested vision-system capability is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is visual observation and recording, excluding manufacturing, sample selection, unrelated laboratory testing and final product release. Shared observation capture must be assigned once.

Production staff produce finished products and quality owners supply existing inspection criteria. Analyst observes and captures findings within the retained 100 hours; no free structured defect code or camera-labelled input is assumed.
Keep native inspection records and current practice. No new classifier, capture process or hardware means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which products and visual criteria are involved
How representative lighting and inspection conditions are established
research_questions: Do inspectors record unexpected or ambiguous observations without treating absence of a known defect code as acceptance?

already_counted.description: Handle and visually inspect products and record observations

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0 and incremental upkeep=0. Physical inspection and observation capture retain full time; no new hardware or production labour saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Capture testing observations, equipment use and inventory movements in the required support documentation
Copy support entries from paper forms into parallel equipment, inventory and testing records
Complete documentation checks, correct discrepancies and accept the testing support record

tasks.design: Configure the existing forms in {OTHER}, the laboratory information management system, so the analyst records support entries once at the activity. Reuse the same controlled record for equipment and inventory views, retaining human completeness and discrepancy checks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper support entries were re-entered into parallel laboratory records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native laboratory records and audit history can support one captured entry with several controlled views.
tasks.still_hard: The system cannot infer that all relevant testing activity was observed or recorded correctly.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows what happened at the bench and recognises gaps or misleading entries.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry where it exists; observation capture and documentation responsibility remain human.

reach.task: Keep traceable bench and equipment records

evidence.claim: SampleManager LIMS tracks samples, assigns tests and logs changes, supporting a check of native traceable laboratory records.
The proposed single-entry equipment and inventory documentation workflow and time savings require local verification.

assumptions: Boundary is support-form, equipment-log and inventory-entry documentation, excluding performing tests, instrument data compilation and report generation. If the laboratory already captures once, s2 offers no saving.

Analyst produces activity identifier, sample or test reference, equipment identifier, activity timestamp, observed entry and unit, inventory item and quantity movement where relevant, form version and author in s1's retained 35 hours. Changing from paper to native entry does not remove capture effort.

Controlled-form owners supply existing field requirements through unchanged quality work; extra configuration upkeep is counted below. Views replacing s2 consume only the captured entry, with no free automatic completeness or discrepancy code.
Missing identifiers, unavailable devices or unsupported forms return to existing manual capture and reconciliation in s3's 40 hours; no record is marked complete from a blank field check alone.
Try native forms and audit history first. Customer quality requirements govern validation; s3 checks entries against actual activities and accepts the exact controlled record.
unknowns: Whether native forms can cover equipment and inventory records without duplication
Which controlled-record and validation requirements apply
research_questions: Can analysts capture once while preserving required correction history and verifying actual activity completeness?

already_counted.description: Capture support fields, verify activities and correct documentation exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain form mappings and retest record views

approvals.approved_version: Exact support record version, form version, equipment and inventory references, corrections and unresolved exceptions; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; subtract 7 focal upkeep for central net=18. Range assumes only some duplicate entry can be removed and fallback forms remain. Two other-role upkeep hours are outside the focal denominator; capture and meaning checks keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile laboratory data and analyze results

steps.what: Select laboratory test data and specify appropriate analysis populations, units and calculations
Compile selected laboratory data and calculate specified summaries and analysis tables
Perform appropriate analyses by checking assumptions, interpreting patterns and investigating data exceptions

tasks.design: Configure repeat data exports and analysis tables in {OTHER}, the laboratory information management system, or its existing {SPREADSHEET} workbook. The analyst chooses appropriate populations and calculations, checks assumptions and interprets results; no model chooses methods or imputes missing measurements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly joining compatible result records and rebuilding the same calculations consumed compilation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed record mappings and versioned formulas can reproduce explicit analysis specifications.
tasks.still_hard: Method differences, missing observations and unusual distributions can invalidate an apparently tidy summary.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst understands when a comparison is scientifically meaningful and when further investigation is needed.
tasks.altitude: Less recurring compilation and arithmetic; analysis choice and interpretation remain human.

reach.task: Evaluate whether analytical summaries support the scientific question

evidence.claim: Fixed data mappings and specified calculations can reproduce repeated analysis tables; method choice and the proposed savings remain unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is analysis-specific compilation and analysis, excluding test execution, support-form entry, established-limit comparison and release recommendations. Each table or comparison action must be owned once across tasks.

Testing staff and instruments produce result records through unchanged testing: sample identifier, method and version, analyte, result, unit, measurement timestamp and source record. Availability in compatible form is a customer condition; additional export-field upkeep is counted below.

Analyst verifies and captures source versions, selected samples, grouping fields, units, explicit formulas, population exclusions, replicate treatment and missing-value rules in s1's 30 hours. Statistical method choice and specification capture are retained human effort.

s2 computes only the chosen summaries. Unmapped fields, censored values, incompatible units or uncertain replicates remain exceptions and return to manual compilation and analysis in s3's 45 hours; there is no automatic imputation or inference of valid data.
Try native exports and workbook configuration first. s3 checks scientific meaning and source provenance as well as arithmetic; customer quality requirements determine validation and acceptance.
unknowns: How many result formats and method versions must be combined
Which analyses are recurring enough to configure
research_questions: Do native configured tables reproduce accepted analyses without hiding method differences or excluded observations?

already_counted.description: Capture analytical definitions, inspect source comparability and interpret results including manual exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain mappings and retest specified calculations

approvals.approved_version: Exact analysis version, source result snapshot, selected population, formulas, exclusions and interpreted limitations; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; subtract 8 focal upkeep for central net=17. Range assumes only recurring compatible tables are configured and many exceptions stay manual. Three other-role upkeep hours are outside focal savings; no testing or scientific interpretation saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated comparison, compilation and duplicate entry may shrink, while observation, scientific interpretation and release recommendations retain human responsibility.
reach: Improve traceable bench records with chemical technicians
skills_to_grow: Specify comparison and analysis inputs precisely
Distinguish numerical flags from data validity
Verify actual activities behind completed records
role.ambitious_version: Produce traceable laboratory evidence with repeatable calculations while keeping scientific and release judgement with qualified people.
